answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes each agent stake a meaningful, slashable deposit tied to one verified identity before it can transact. The deposit is locked in escrow and forfeited if the agent is caught voting twice, spamming, or farming rewards, so creating thousands of hollow sock-puppet accounts becomes a marble-hard expense instead of a free trick. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest, while the nebula of fake identities collapses because each one costs real money to mint and risks losing it. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defender.
